messages:
alex: heads-up — noticed a perf regression after yesterday's canary deployment. multiple consoles reporting slow charts and janky interactions. p95 main-thread blocking up ~3-4x compared to last week. :eyes:

maria: which canary? link?

alex: canary id from ui-ci-bot is 2026-03-19T21:10Z, hash ab12c. throwing telemetry traces in #telemetry but putting the quick snapshot here.

alex: ```
main_thread_blocking_ms: p50=120, p95=420, p99=1220
bundle_size_main.js: 1.8MB -> 2.6MB (+45%)
chart-init (render+hydrate): avg 80ms -> 430ms
kv-cache miss rate on heatmap: +12%
```

benjamin: saw this locally after pulling that canary. profiler points at chart-entry path — a new dependency landed in vendor chunk: plotly-lite (PR #482).

maria: oh right, PR #482 was the interactive axis labels enhancement. it imported plotly-lite at top-level instead of lazy-loading.

kevin: that explains bundle bump. options: 1) rollback PR 482 from canary 2) lazy-load plotly only for advanced widgets 3) split vendor chunk to separate heavy libs.

benjamin: i reverted PR 482 locally and perf returned to baseline (p95 main-blocking ~140ms). can confirm its the culprit.

maria: can we do a quick rollback to canary and re-run canary tests? prefer rollback then ship a lazy-load patch.

alex: +1 rollback now, then small follow-up to lazy-load. also want a console-only feature flag to gate new axis labels.

kevin: i'll open rollback PR and a short changelog entry. can we avoid revving the large vendor chunk this week? release windows are tight.

maria: i'll prepare the lazy-load patch. suggestion: dynamic import at component mount: const Plotly = await import('plotly-lite'); keep SSR path minimal.

benjamin: small note — telemetry ingestion spiked when charts tried to render failing KV cache hits. sre-bot, did we get any alerts?

sre-bot: observed increased frontend error rate (1.5% -> 3.9%) and telemetry write spikes between 21:12-21:30Z. no infra CPU or GPU saturation. routing/quotas unchanged.

alex: good to know not infra. action items: kevin rollback canary (assign kevin), maria lazy-load patch + flag (assign maria), ben to validate metrics post-rollback, alex will coordinate canary smoke tests.

kevin: rollback PR opened -> https://git.internal/r/rollback-482 (deploystage: canary). triggering canary now.

ui-ci-bot: deployment started for rollback-482 to canary at 21:37Z. watch http://ci.internal/canary/2387654321

benjamin: smoke run in progress, initial dashboard renders look back to normal speed. will post final numbers in 5m.

maria: thanks all. after rollback we should add a bundling rule to flag new deps >200KB and require lazy-load justification in PR template.

alex: agreed — create ticket for bundling guardrails and a size budget check in CI.

benjamin: final numbers after rollback: main_thread_blocking_ms p95=150, bundle_main.js back to 1.79MB. heatmap kv miss back to baseline.

alex: closing loop — rollback successful. follow-ups tracked in GH issues. thanks :thumbsup:
